explanations: The Pacific is the largest and deepest division, and holds the Challenger Deep, the deepest known point in the world.
The Atlantic is the second largest, an elongated S-shaped basin between the Americas and Europe and Africa, first crossed by the Norse.
The Indian is the third largest and the warmest, bounded by Asia, Africa and Australia, with a climate ruled by the monsoon.
Pacific, Atlantic and Indian are three of the five oceans into which one body of salt water, covering 70.8 per cent of Earth, is conventionally divided.

sources.excerpt: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's five oceanic divisions.
The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, located in the northwestern Pacific, is the deepest known point in the world, reaching a depth of 10,928 m (35,853 ft).
The Atlantic Ocean is the second largest of the world's five oceans, with an area of about 85,133,000 square kilometers (32,870,000 sq mi).
The Atlantic Ocean occupies an elongated, S-shaped basin extending longitudinally between Europe and Africa to the east, and the Americas to the west.
While the Norse were the first known humans to cross the Atlantic, it was the expedition of Christopher Columbus in 1492 that proved to be the most consequential.
The Indian Ocean is the third-largest of the world's five oceanic divisions, covering 70,560,000 km2 (27,240,000 sq mi) or approximately 20% of the water area of Earth's surface.
It is the warmest ocean, with a significant impact on global climate due to its interaction with the atmosphere.
It is bounded by Asia to the north, Africa to the west and Australia to the east.
The climate around the Indian Ocean is characterized by monsoons.

The ocean is conventionally divided into large bodies of water, which are also referred to as oceans (in descending order by area: the Pacific Ocean, the Atlantic Ocean, the Indian Ocean, the Antarctic/Southern Ocean, and the Arctic Ocean), and are themselves mostly divided into seas, gulfs and subsequent bodies of water.
